# v1 alpha: close the gap

Local only, never PR it. Written 2026-11-17 from three Codex reports (`docs/research/2026-11-17-*.json`, untracked), the Codex adversarial audit (`/tmp/callisto-adversarial-audit-2026-11-17/`), the Changesets v3 announcement, migration and automation guides, e18e's publishing guide, and three read-only verification lanes at `ab3c030`. Every finding below was confirmed in source (file:line); the load-bearing ones were re-read by hand. Nothing was built or changed.

## Root causes, not findings

Twenty findings reduce to seven model flaws. Fix the flaw and the findings cannot come back; patch the findings and they will.

| # | Flaw | Findings it produces | Structural fix (first rung that works) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | "Is there releasable input" is not a value. Each consumer rebuilds it from a stand-in: the winning `named_by`, a count of resolvable changeset files, `consumed` being empty, a deleted `.md` in the merged diff | F02 retained prerelease note erases fresh inference (`aggregate.rs:325-392`, also drops group and dependent bumps); F03 invalid notes become a green no-op (`release_pr.rs:112`, script `:78-81`); inferred-only changes never open a release PR; pre-mode decide loop (retained notes keep `has_changesets` true forever); E165 `NoChangesetConsumed` (`release_decision.rs:483`); `version.rs:351-359` empty check; `InferredReleaseWithoutChangeset` warning; dead `CascadeInput.named_by` (`cascade.rs:137`); `reason_from_bump` maps `None` to `Changeset` (`release_decision.rs:957`) | `Seed { severity, sources: NonEmpty<Source> }`, `enum Source { FreshChangeset, RetainedChangeset, Inference, Group }`; severity is the max, "fresh" is an exhaustive match. `ReleasePrDecisionV2::derive` takes a `PendingRelease` with a private constructor built only from a strictly loaded `VersionPlan`; the `bool` goes. The decision records `consumed_changesets`, so E165 compares sets |
| R2 | Native identity is a raw `String`; normalization is free helpers some callers apply | F01 high: PEP 503-equivalent PyPI names admitted as two owners (`walk.rs:298`), one upload, both tags. Sibling: crates.io `-`/`_`/case (`package_id.rs:189`). Selector `pypi/my-pkg` gets E102 while dependency resolution matches (`identity.rs:404`). Config rules, tags, `add` compare raw | `NativeName` in `callisto-model::identity`: private field, `new(Ecosystem, &str)`, keeps display spelling, `Eq/Hash/Ord` on the canonical key (PyPI PEP 503, Cargo lowercase with `_`->`-`, npm exact). `native_owner`, `IdentityIndex.native`, `ReleasePackageId.name`, config rule matching key on it |
| R3 | Values lose structure at boundaries: refs, YAML scalars, HTTP framing, input origin travel as `&str` | F04 `last_ref_segment` takes the last `/` (`init.rs:734`, two callers); F05 seven raw `replace()` into YAML (`init.rs:902-909`), `__COMMIT__` never parsed as `CommitSha`; F06 `rsplit_once("\r\n\r\n")` truncates a body with a blank line (`http.rs:56`; fails loudly); F10 every JSON parse error is E281/usage and paths ignore `--cwd` (`io.rs:19`); `checkpoint.rs` trailer search, `ls-tree` without `-z` | `BranchName` (only `from_full_ref` or `git check-ref-format --branch`); one `WorkflowScalar` encoder that `render_workflow` requires by type; header-first HTTP parse; `enum JsonInput { Stdin, Inline, File(PathBuf) }` through `resolve_file_arg` |
| R4 | One resolution, two implementations, no index | F07 O(E x P) relative `workspace:` lookup (`walk.rs:34-68,776`; 12x at 800 packages); `npm.rs:92-113` resolves the same path again and swallows errors | Canonical-dir -> `PackageId` index built once; both callers use it |
| R5 | Checks that cannot fail | F08 `! cargo tree | grep` passes when cargo fails (`justfile:99,111`); `coverage-per-crate` passes on empty data; bench prints "failed" and exits 0; flaky graph test is fixture portability (bsdtar `._*` with xattrs, bare `cargo` from PATH) | Boundaries move into `deny.toml`; `set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]`; bench exits 1; fixture uses `$CARGO` and `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1` |
| R6 | Wire compatibility assumed, not modeled | v3 `pre.json` (`{mode, tag}`) fails to parse (`pre.rs:106-133`); callisto writes v2 only, drops unknown keys; `.changeset/pre/` ignored and a move there fails E165 `UnexpectedPath`; ADR 1 says "same shape" | `enum PreStateShape { V2, V3 }` read from the file, written back in the shape read. Retained notes become `Source::RetainedChangeset` whichever shape stored them |
| R7 | Publish credentials and untrusted code share a process or job | Simple template: one `release` job builds and publishes with `id-token: write`; matrix `build` job runs project build code with `id-token: write` (for attestations); npm publish runs from the source directory, so lifecycle scripts run inside the process that holds npm's OIDC variables | Pack, then publish the tarball with `--ignore-scripts` in a job that runs no project code; attestation in its own job over uploaded artifacts; `id-token` only on that job and the publish job |

R1 and R6 meet: v3's split (root = fresh, `pre/` = retained) is the fresh/retained distinction R1 introduces. Build `Source` first; v3 support is then mostly storage. R7 must land before OIDC: with trusted publishing, a job holding `id-token` that runs build code can mint a publish token, because npm's trust is per workflow file unless bound to an environment, and this repo's policy forbids environments.

## Changesets v3: what changed and where Callisto stands

| v3 change | Callisto today | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Peer dependents get a patch, not a major; authors add an explicit major when needed | Out-of-range peer + minor/major source -> Major when `peer-escalation = true`, the default (`cascade.rs:46-52`). That is v2's behaviour | Flip the default to `false` (the dependent then gets `cascade.bump-severity`, patch). Owner decision; a default change ships as **Breaking** |
| Dev-dependency ranges rewritten without releasing the owner | Cascade never follows dev edges; an unrewritable dev range is left with a warning (`cascade.rs:437,612`) | Add the scenario test (a 1.0.0->2.0.0, b dev `^1`): range rewritten, b not released |
| Build, pack, publish as separate jobs; `id-token` only on publish (e18e standard workflow) | Matrix: separate `build` and `execute`, but `build` holds `id-token`. Simple: one job | R7 (WP L) |
| Pre mode: consumed notes move to `.changeset/pre/`, `pre.json` drops ids, auto-migrates on `status` | v2 shape only; v3 repos fail | R6 (WP G). Read both, write the shape read; no silent migration |
| `changeset status --since=<ref>` exits 1 when changed packages lack changesets; `changeset --empty` | No equivalent; `status --check` gates errors only | WP M: one diagnostic in `status` over changed packages, gated by an existing exit path. New flag only with owner confirmation |
| `version` exits 1 with no unreleased changesets | No changesets is an error only under `--strict` | Keep. Callisto's `release-pr decide` is the automation entry point, so a script never runs `version` blind |
| `add --major/--minor/--patch --message` | `add --package <id>:<bump> --summary` already non-interactive | None |
| Private packages not versioned or tagged by default (`privatePackages`) | Private npm workspace root skipped; other private packages versioned | Check and document in the migration page; change only if a user hits it |
| `baseBranch` defaults to `main`; `tag` renamed `git-tag`; `access: private` -> `restricted` | `init` ignores `baseBranch` and `access` with a warning | Migration (WP K) |
| Changelog formatting through the project's formatter (prettier, oxfmt, deno, dprint) | Callisto renders its own Markdown | None |
| Staged npm publishing | Not supported; v3 does not support it either | Defer; separate decision |
| Release PR through a GitHub App token so CI runs on it | Action takes a token input (not checked) | Check in WP L; document |

## Map to the gap analysis

The positioning is "reviewable, dependency-aware releases with recovery from partial failures". F01 (a wrong `alreadySatisfied` adoption), F02 and F03 (silent omissions) sit inside that claim, so they come before any evidence is published.

| Gap | Covered by |
| --- | --- |
| 1 Tokenless publishing | L, J; real proof in R |
| 2 Managed prerelease | F1, F2, G, H |
| 3 Inferred-only release PRs | F1, F2 |
| 4 Contributor coverage check | M |
| 5 Changesets v2/v3 migration | G, K, N |
| 6 Python fit (co-located Maturin, private/HTML PyPI) | Out of alpha scope (after v1) |
| 7 Windows, other forges | Out of alpha scope |
| 8 Readiness evidence (recovery, registry binding, native matrix, onboarding) | Q, R |
| Recovery and integrity defects found since | E (F01), F1/F2 (F02, F03), B (F06) |
| Rust evaluation (unused `tracing`, `homepage`) | A |
| External validation (five owners, Sampo head-to-head) | After H and Q; owner-run |

## Product gaps from the landscape research

- Managed prerelease: owner said yes (crucial for our own releases). Unblocked by R1 + R6; then delete `reject_pre_mode` and E318.
- Inferred-only release PRs: falls out of R1 (`PendingRelease` from the post-cascade plan). Opt-in per package through the existing `release-trigger`; no new key. ADR 2 does not forbid it; its consequence bullet and specs `release.json:368`, `cli.json:191` change.
- OIDC through native tools, after R7: add `twine` + `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` to `credentials_needed_by` (`runner.rs:82`); `PYPI_TOKEN` optional in init; a pinned `crates-io-auth-action` step feeding `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`; fix `OIDC-TRUSTED-PUBLISHING.md` lines 21, 22, 24. No config key. Tokenless publish stays unproven until run against real registries.
- Changesets v2 and v3 migration: R6, then `init` translation of `linked`/`ignore`/`access`/`baseBranch` where an equivalent exists, and a page listing semantic differences (linked groups bump every live member; peer policy; private packages).
- Hygiene: delete workspace `tracing`; drop `homepage` (equal to `repository`; Cargo 1.100 warns).

## Pushback

- No Tokio, plugin framework, trait-per-concern rewrite or execution journal. Every finding is a lost value, a duplicated rule or a shared trust boundary: a type, an index or a job split fixes each.
- e18e recommends a protected GitHub Environment with required reviewers. This repo's policy forbids it; R7 gets most of the benefit by keeping `id-token` off every job that runs project code. Binding trusted publishers to an environment stays the owner's call.
- No unwrap lint move: measured 806 errors in integration-test helpers; the `justfile` shape works.
- No toolchain pin yet: CI's toolchain comes from `orin-dx/actions/setup-rust` (not read). Locally `stable` is 1.98.1, a session override pins 1.99.1, 1.100.0 is current; clippy is clean on 1.100.0.
- F06 is lower than the audit's medium: it fails loudly, only with pretty-printed bodies.
- No plan-comparison command for migration until its value is measured.
- "No ceremony" keeps what the ruleset enforces: signed commits, trails, changesets for released-behaviour fixes, exit-code gates.
- AGENTS.md forbids parallel cargo builds. Swarm parallelism is in reading, design and editing; builds take one machine-wide lock. Relaxing that is the owner's call.

## Work packages

Changeset = fix to released behaviour or a default change.

| WP | Scope | Files (overlap risk) | Changeset | Model / effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | R5 gates + hygiene | `justfile`, `deny.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, bench, `provider/registry/tests.rs` | no | Sonnet, medium |
| B | F06 HTTP parser | `provider/http.rs` | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| C | F10 typed JSON input | `cli/io.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs` (args only) | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| D | R3 init boundary: `BranchName`, `WorkflowScalar`, `CommitSha` for `__COMMIT__`, F09 hint and E278 help | `graph/commands/init.rs`, templates, `cli/commands/init.rs` | yes | Opus, medium |
| E | R2 `NativeName` | `model/identity.rs`, `package_id.rs`, `walk.rs` admission, `identity.rs`, `config/resolve.rs`, `tags.rs`, `release_decision.rs:28-44` | yes | Opus, high |
| F1 | R1 `Seed`/`Source` in aggregation | `aggregate.rs`, `cascade.rs`, `version.rs`, `status.rs` | yes (F02) | Opus, high |
| F2 | R1 `PendingRelease`, decision `consumed_changesets`, E165 sets; inferred release PRs; F03 | `model/release_pr.rs`, `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, `release_decision.rs`, `model/release/decision.rs`, action script, ADR 2, specs, `wire-compat.md` | yes | Opus, high |
| G | R6 `pre.json` v2/v3 + `pre/` archive | `model/format/pre.rs`, `aggregate.rs` listing, `release_decision.rs` allowed paths, ADR 1 | yes | Opus, medium |
| H | Managed prerelease: delete E318, release-PR loop over a pre cycle, lifecycle test | `cli/commands/release_pr.rs`, action script, specs, `errors.md` | yes | Opus, high |
| I | R4 dir index (F07) + pnpm-relative bench shape | `walk.rs` edges, `manifests/npm.rs`, `fixtures/perf.rs` | yes | Sonnet, high |
| L | R7 publish isolation: pack then publish tarball with `--ignore-scripts`; simple template split into build and publish jobs; attestation job; `id-token` only where needed | `registry_argv.rs`, npm provider, templates, `init.rs`, this repo's release workflow + policy script | yes | Opus, high |
| J | OIDC native (after L) | `cli/runner.rs`, init templates, docs | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| K | Migration v2/v3: init translation + docs | `graph/commands/init.rs` key table, docs | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| M | Changed-without-changeset check (v3 `status --since`) | `status.rs`, `cli.rs` | yes | Sonnet, medium |
| N | Peer default to v3 policy + dev-edge scenario test | `config` defaults, `docs/config.md`, cascade tests | yes (Breaking) | Sonnet, medium |

| Q | Recovery evidence, the positioning claim: a local `just verify-real` harness against local registries (npm verdaccio-style, `cargo-http-registry`, a local PyPI) rehearsing partial publish -> rerun adopts, delayed visibility, conflicting tag, missing Python artifact; production registry binding for Cargo/PyPI (`registry_endpoint.rs` rejects non-https loopback, so the harness needs a test-only allowance decided first); the native install/load matrix recorded from `native_resolution_e2e_tests` | `registry_endpoint.rs`, new harness, docs | no | Opus, high |
| R | Onboarding time and tokenless publish against real registries | needs owner accounts | no | owner + Sonnet |

Investigations (read-only, any time): GH token stripped from native git vs `gh auth git-credential` (needs a clean Linux runner); process-tree cancellation and unbounded output in `run`; multi-distribution prerequisite edges; Sampo head-to-head on one mixed workspace after H.

## Waves

- Wave 0 (now, disjoint files): A, B, C.
- Wave 1: D, E, F1. E and F1 both touch `release_decision.rs` at different ranges: `git merge-tree` before the second merges.
- Wave 2 (critical path, serial): F2 -> G -> H. In parallel: I (after E, shares `walk.rs`), L (after D, shares templates and `init.rs`), N.
- Wave 3: J (after L), K (after G), M (after F2, shares `status.rs`), Q (after E and F2, so it rehearses the fixed model).
- Wave 4: R, then the external pilot.

Critical path: F1 -> F2 -> G -> H. Second chain: D -> L -> J.

## How the swarm runs

- One named worktree per WP, branch off `main`, no stacks; merge in wave order.
- Builds: each worktree has its own target dir; every cargo invocation takes one machine-wide lock (`flock $TMPDIR/callisto-cargo.lock cargo ...`), so agents overlap on thinking and editing, never on builds.
- Per WP: the implementer writes the regression first, driving the real binary or function at the boundary named in the finding, then the type change, then deletes checks the type now covers.
- Proof by exit code: `just pre-push && just lint && just doc-check && just test`; `cargo mutants --in-diff` on the WP diff with zero missed except argued equivalents (it found two real gaps on a caliper branch today); sibling sweep listed in the PR body.
- Review: one fresh-context Opus reviewer per WP, given the diff and the finding, not the implementer's reasoning.
- Gates run unsandboxed in the worktree: sandboxed runs fail tests that write inside the repo and look like defects.
- Ship: signed commit, changeset via `callisto add`, push, link a trail (#357 for A-E, I; #250 or a new prerelease trail for F-H, K, M, N; a new publish-security trail for L, J).
- Orchestration: a Workflow script can run each wave as a pipeline (implement -> mutate -> review -> gate), with the build lock as the only shared resource; it needs an explicit "use a workflow".

## Alpha scope (planning only, not documented)

GitHub-hosted, Linux/macOS, Cargo + npm (napi-rs included), separate-directory Python. Out: Windows, other forges, co-located Maturin, private/HTML PyPI, staged npm publish.

## Settled decisions

Decided; sessions do not ask.

1. ADR 2's consequence bullet amended: inferred-only release PRs allowed through `release-trigger`.
2. Decision schema v3 with `consumed_changesets`; readers accept 1-3.
3. `pre.json` written back in the shape read.
4. Cargo `foo-bar`/`foo_bar` in one workspace is E100.
5. `init --workflow` adds the workflow when `callisto.toml` exists.
6. OIDC before 1.0, after R7, with `id-token: write` on this repo's `execute` job.
7. Peer default moves to v3's patch policy, shipped as Breaking.
8. One changed-without-changeset flag on `status`.
9. Builds run in parallel across worktrees (each has its own `target/`); never two in one worktree. WP A rewords AGENTS.md's "Never run cargo builds in parallel" to say "in the same checkout".

## Where the owner is needed

- Launching the sessions.
- Merging PRs (sessions never merge), in wave order.
- Registry accounts for R (tokenless publish, onboarding time) and the external pilot.
# v1 alpha: session launch prompts

Local only. Plan: `.claude/plans/PLAN-v1-alpha-close-the-gap.md`. Open each session in `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto`, set model and effort, paste the prompt. Sessions run unattended; they come back to you only to merge.

| Session | Work | `/model` | `/effort` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Release model | F1 -> F2 -> G -> H -> M | Opus 5.5 | medium |
| 2 Publish chain | D -> L -> J | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 3 Fixes | A, B, C (workflow), then K (after G merges) and N | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 5 Identity and graph | E -> I | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |
| 4 Evidence (after E and F2 merge) | Q | Sonnet 5.5 | medium |

Opus spend is limited to Session 1 (one cross-cutting semantic change, where a rework loop costs more than Opus) and to subagents: an Opus design note at the start of L, E and Q, and the Opus reviewer per PR.

Capacity: disk is the limit (about 98 GB free; stale worktree `target/` dirs hold about 89 GB, all regenerable). With debug info off, expect a few GB per active worktree. Sessions 1, 3 (three Wave 0 worktrees) and 5 build at once from the start; Session 2 starts with them because J's first change is tiny, and its heavier builds overlap Wave 0 finishing.

Before launch, free the stale build output (build artifacts only, no source or branches touched):

```

claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 2 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Use a workflow: run Session 3 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
claude --bg --model sonnet --effort medium "Run Session 5 in .claude/plans/LAUNCH-v1-alpha-sessions.md."
```

## Rules

- Before each WP: `git fetch`; re-verify the plan's finding against current main (other sessions merge in between). If another session already owns the WP's branch, skip to your next WP.
- Work in a named worktree per WP (EnterWorktree), branched off origin/main. No stacks. Each worktree builds into its own `target/`, so builds in different worktrees run in parallel with no lock; never run two builds in the same worktree.
- Build budget, exported once per session: `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0` (debug info is most of each `target/`; dropping it cuts disk and link time), `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$(( $(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) / 4 ))` and the same value for nextest `--test-threads`, so four builders share the CPU.
- Mutation testing runs in place in the WP worktree after committing: `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <diff>`; it reuses the worktree's `target/` instead of copying the tree.
- Start independent pieces early in their own worktrees: Session 1 runs G's `pre.json` reader/writer (`model/format/pre.rs`) as a subagent with `isolation: "worktree"` while it works on F1; Session 2 ships J's twine environment change (`runner.rs`) first. Only the parts that touch shared files wait for their chain.
- Start the reviewer subagent as soon as the diff is final, in parallel with the gate and mutation run; it reads, it never builds.
- When a WP's PR is open and green, `rm -rf <worktree>/target`; after merge, remove the worktree and its local branch.

result.output:
Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for simple workspaces. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).
---
## Where a publish goes

A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm and `.cargo/config.toml` for Cargo. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means those files decide where the registry token is sent. Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. For npm (except yarn) and PyPI, set `url` on the registry entry to pin the destination in `callisto.toml`; Cargo takes its destination only from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a `url` on a cargo registry is rejected.

---

## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.

1	**Callisto QA swarm — 18 November 2026**
2	
3	Six new confirmed defects: **one high, four medium and one low**, including one confirmed performance defect. Every finding has an independent validation pass. Final correctness reproductions use a newly built binary from frozen revision `fac8cadf91f792fdd17dec93d36eeb10be24e5f3`.
4	
5	The live checkout advanced from `ab3c030` while discovery ran. I preserved those external merges, archived the newer source into `source-fac8cadf91/`, built it in `current-build/`, and repeated the findings against that binary. Initial discovery and some exploratory optimized benchmarks used the older binary; they are explicitly distinguished below. No implementation changes, commits, pushes or registry/forge effects were made by this audit. All audit artifacts remain outside the public repository.
6	
7	**Complete new finding list**
8	
9	| ID | Severity | Finding | Current source anchor |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| QA-01 | High | Interrupted version recovery can apply a sibling workspace's plan | [checkpoint.rs:198](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/checkpoint.rs:198) |
12	| QA-02 | Medium | Python requirement rewrites drop epochs and weaken constraints | [python.rs:823](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:823) |
13	| QA-03 | Medium | Terminal `*` in a package directory selects sibling commits | [access.rs:700](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:700) |
14	| QA-04 | Low | A valid record-separator character in a commit body stops inference | [access.rs:907](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/vcs/access.rs:907) |
15	| QA-05 | Medium | Publication dependencies leak across an owner's native outputs | [derive.rs:503](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:503) |
16	| QA-06 | Medium | Historical ownership checks repeat Git probes for the same commit | [tags.rs:259](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs:259) |
17	
18	Source links point into the live checkout and can move. The immutable inspected copies are under `source-fac8cadf91/` alongside this report.
19	
20	**QA-01 — Recovery can successfully apply the wrong workspace plan. CONFIRMED.**
21	
22	An independent fixture contains sibling directories `  release-work` and `release-work`. The first owns `primary-package`3.4.5 with a patch changeset; the second owns `other-package`3.4.5 with a minor changeset. An ordinary dry run correctly proposes primary3.4.6. The test interrupts the real CLI immediately after successful checkpoint creation, before version writes, then retries.
23	
24	The retry exits0 but reports other-package3.5.0, writes3.5.0 into the primary manifest, consumes the primary patch note, and writes a primary-directory changelog headed `other-package` with the sibling's minor note. The actual sibling remains unchanged. Root reproduced this again on the frozen current binary; `recovery-current/independent-results.json` and `replay.log` contain the before/interruption/after sequence.
25	
26	The first loss is `git_stdout_env` using `stdout_trimmed` for a path. Both the recorded and current workspace prefix lose their leading spaces, so their equality check still passes. `open_checkpoint_tree` then opens the trimmed sibling in the scratch tree. Existing input/version guards can pass because the original files and starting versions match; they do not bind the scratch plan's package roster to the final apply root. ApplyPermit authorizes a write but does not establish that it belongs to the planned workspace.
27	
28	Controls: a normal prefix recovers correctly; missing trimmed sibling refuses E213; a sibling with a different starting version refuses E117. The incorrect success requires the colliding workspace/path/version conditions, not any workspace crash. Leading tabs also fail path recovery. This is a local data-integrity bug; no remote publishing scenario is claimed.
29	
30	Correction direction: preserve native path bytes, removing only the protocol terminator, and verify exact checkpoint/scratch/apply workspace identity plus package roster before mutation. The regression should assert final package identity, version, note consumption and changelog, not only successful retry. Independent report: [recovery validation](validation-recovery/report.md).
31	
32	**QA-02 — Native version data survives the bump but disappears from the requirement. CONFIRMED.**
33	
34	A Python package at `2!0.4.8` patch-releases to `2!0.4.9`. Its co-released dependent's supported `>=2!0.4.8` declaration becomes `>=0.4.9`. The CLI exits0. Independent pip-packaging evaluation proves an epoch-zero version such as99.0.0 was rejected before and accepted after; the old dependency version remains accepted too. An epoch-zero control raises its floor correctly.
35	
36	`render_target` reconstructs a stable target from major/minor/patch, omitting PEP440 epoch. Native bump arithmetic correctly retains the epoch. Checking only whether the new target satisfies the rewritten requirement is too weak: a wider, wrong range still contains that target.
37	
38	The discovery matrix used seed180026,32 version/requirement cases, supported operators and optional extras/markers.26 commands succeeded;13 successful cases failed the semantic oracle. These are related manifestations, not13 independent bugs. Exact epoch pins also produced E319 rather than a valid rewrite in some cases. Runtime and optional-extra sites share the renderer; compatible-release and upper-bound renderers need the same sibling review. Poetry input is not claimed independently verified.
39	
40	Correction direction: render using native PEP440 semantics, preserving epoch and intended precision. Assert both target inclusion and preservation of forbidden older versions. Independent current-binary evidence: [semantic/path validation](validation-semantics-paths/report.md), `current-binary-validation.json`; discovery/minimal repro: [semantic campaign](semantics/report.md).
41	
42	**QA-03 — A filesystem identity is reinterpreted as a Git pattern. CONFIRMED.**
43	
44	With packages under `packages/odd*` and `packages/odd-other`, a fix committed only to the sibling makes automatic inference patch-release both. Native `git log` using a literal pathspec returns no history for the untouched owner; the raw pathspec used by Callisto includes the sibling's commit. An own-only control bumps only the owner. An interior-star example did not reproduce the false positive, so this report identifies the proven terminal-star trigger precisely.
45	
46	`commits_since` passes package directories directly after `--`. That terminates options but does not disable Git pathspec wildcard semantics. `first_parent_commits_touching` is a structurally related raw-path caller. Other change-listing code already has literal-path treatment, so the contract is inconsistent between sibling operations.
47	
48	Correction direction: centralize literal package-path arguments at the Git boundary and migrate all callers whose inputs are filesystem identities. Test an untouched wildcard-named directory alongside a touched sibling, using native literal Git history as oracle. Evidence: [independent current-binary results](validation-semantics-paths/current-binary-validation.json).
49	
50	**QA-04 — Message data collides with record framing. CONFIRMED.**
51	
52	An otherwise ordinary `fix:` commit whose body contains U+001E causes `version --dry-run` to fail E026 while reading history. Ordinary-text and U+001F controls infer the expected patch. The current binary was independently tested; no alternate records or hostile messages were constructed.
53	
54	Git accepts the body character. Callisto emits full message data inside a custom separator format and later splits on that same unescaped separator. The parser fails closed, so the demonstrated impact is blocked automatic inference, not incorrect publication or code execution. Severity is Low because the trigger is unusual.
55	
56	Correction direction: use unambiguous record framing and preserve body content. Keep this boundary regression separate from tests that only feed malformed synthetic backend output. Source trace and controls are in [semantic/path validation](validation-semantics-paths/report.md).
57	
58	**QA-05 — Native dependency context is lost during publication graph projection. CONFIRMED.**
59	
60	For dual Cargo/npm owners A and B, a Cargo-only dependency A→B is attached not only to Cargo A's publication but also to npm A's publication. Independent reverse controls show an npm-only edge also ordering the unrelated Cargo output. Fresh fixtures with distinct native names reproduce both on the frozen current binary.
61	
62	`link_publish_prerequisites` loops over every selected output, then every dependency of its owner. It filters the dependency destination by the declaring manifest's ecosystem, but never filters whether the selected dependent output belongs to that ecosystem. Accepted ADR12 and the current-behavior portion of the polyglot architecture require distribution-context publication edges. Shared tags correctly remain owner-level barriers; that does not authorize copying native prerequisites to all outputs.
63	
64	Opposing native edges also expose a related ambiguity: independently acyclic Cargo/npm graphs can be rejected as an owner cycle. The current release spec explicitly rejects package-level runtime/build/optional cycles, so this cycle behavior is recorded as model/spec tension, not a second confirmed defect or a newly invented gate.
65	
66	Correction direction: retain declaring distribution context when projecting native edges. Resolve owner-level cycle policy explicitly before changing it. Independent source/contract adjudication: [architecture report](validation-architecture/report.md), `current-fac8-results.json`.
67	
68	**QA-06 — Equivalent historical queries are repeated for every tag. CONFIRMED.**
69	
70	A repository originally contains a Cargo package, then replaces it with a same-named npm package. All old annotated version tags point to one old commit. Correct behavior rejects those tags as foreign. The defect is the cost: each different tag name misses historical caches even though its tree is identical, and selection starts over on a shrinking candidate list.
71	
72	Independent command-count fixtures confirmed the pattern. Root expanded it on the current binary. One package, one historical source commit and unchanged working tree:
73	
74	| Rejected historical tags | Git processes | Native median wall time |
75	| ---: | ---: | ---: |
76	|1|10|176ms|
77	|10|64|622ms|
78	|50|304|2,993ms|
79	
80	Process counts used a transparent logging wrapper; wall times were measured separately without that wrapper, three runs per cell. The wrapped runs are not used as production latency evidence. Raw records: `perf/foreign-measured/foreign-tag-results.json` and `native-wall-results.json`. Independent smaller controls: `validation-architecture/foreign-tags/results.json`.
81	
82	The observed process formula is6T+4 for these fixtures. `Rosters` uses raw tag strings in `(rev,path)` and `(rev,name)` keys, so same-commit tags repeat identical historical probes. The rejection loop also reparses T+(T−1)+…+1 candidates. A constant process count on ordinary tag layouts does not cover this ownership-migration shape.
83	
84	Correction direction: batch tag peeling, key immutable history caches by commit identity, and parse/order candidate versions once before checking ownership. Preserve version/tag-name tie-breaking and historical ownership rules. Parallelizing repeated queries would retain the underlying defect.
85	
86	A separate explicit-shared-template path reparses identical candidates per package. It is a low-priority optimization, not a seventh primary defect: the whole-CLI measurement was619ms for500 packages sharing5000 tags, and does not isolate parser CPU. Cache semantic selection by exact template and grammar only for name-only selection; ownership-filtered paths need their own context. Detailed caveats: [performance adjudication](validation-architecture/performance-adjudication.md).
87	
88	**How the swarm worked**
89	
90	Three discovery agents partitioned failure modes across the workspace: semantic ordering/native requirements, boundary/parser behavior, and crash/retry recovery. Three separate validation roles reconstructed cases, tried negative controls and adjudicated contracts. Root owned builds, coverage-guided fuzzing, performance measurements, revision freezing and final classification. Six agents participated across the two waves; this was not six simultaneous Cargo builds. Cargo builds remained serialized.
91	
92	The campaign used industry failure patterns as test strategies: native grammar differential oracles; graph closure and permutation invariants; valid awkward paths; delimiter/data separation; interruption after acknowledgment but before subsequent writes; stale/wrong-context evidence; and immutable-identity cache keys. These patterns generated candidates, not conclusions. Every confirmed finding has a concrete source-to-observable-outcome trace and a sibling sweep.
93	
94	Three agent turns stopped with tool-side content-filter errors. Their saved evidence was not accepted blindly: successful independent roles and root reconstructed the benign regression cases. No additional exploitation work was pursued. A21-row broad fault-injection harness had a SyntaxError in its shim; all21 rows are excluded from product test coverage. The valid checkpoint scenarios were separately rebuilt and executed. An initial Python-oracle harness parsing error is likewise excluded; the corrected32-case campaign is the one counted.
95	
96	**Fuzzing and executed evidence**
97	
98	| Campaign | Executed result | Oracle / scope |
99	| --- | --- | --- |
100	| Manifest editor libFuzzer |90,613 inputs, exit0|Open or clean error; successful write must parse/read back its target|
101	| Manifest identity libFuzzer |213,660 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
102	| Changeset parser libFuzzer |467,578 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
103	| Package-id parser libFuzzer |565,938 inputs, exit0|Parser must return or reject without crashing|
104	| Python semantic generator |32 cases, seed180026|Independent pip-packaging requirement/version semantics|
105	| Graph/permutation generator |48 discovery-revision dry runs, seed181126; no mismatches|Independent monotone closure oracle over24 six-node DAGs, each permuted|
106	| Boundary campaigns |Depth, pathspec and8 message-body character controls|Current contract plus native Git literal/history behavior|
107	| Recovery validation |Four independent original fixtures plus fresh current-binary crash/retry replay|Manifest identity/version, notes, changelog and sibling state|
108	| Native publication graph |Three independent fixtures, repeated on current binary|Accepted distribution-level ordering contract|
109	| Performance |Same-commit foreign-tag counts and separate native timings|Identical history/tree state, varying tag aliases|
110	
111	The48 graph/permutation controls ran on the initial discovery binary; the newer revision changes peer policy, so those passing controls are not represented as current-revision validation. The reported defects were separately reproduced on the current binary.
112	
113	Total coverage-guided inputs: **1,337,789**, with no crash observed. These are bounded smoke campaigns, not an assurance of crash freedom. Seed181126, maximum configured input8192 bytes, bounded per-input time and memory were recorded in the commands/logs. The manifest editor ran30 seconds; the other targets12 seconds each (libFuzzer reported31/13-second elapsed totals).
114	
115	The original macOS fuzz build first hit a restricted shared-cache download, then a sanitizer-coverage link failure from `pep440_rs`'s auxiliary cdylib target. The successful isolated harness used offline cached dependencies and a temporary copy of the same dependency source with only the unused cdylib build target removed. No algorithm source changed. Sanitizer mode was `none`; coverage feedback and debug/overflow assertions were enabled. Do not describe this as an ASan run. Fuzz sources point to the frozen current Callisto source. Logs, corpus, command metadata and adaptation are retained in `fuzz/`, `corpus/` and `fuzz-summary.json`.
116	
117	This explains why semantic fuzzing mattered: a crash fuzzer can pass while a successful command weakens a constraint, selects the wrong directory or applies the wrong plan. Stronger state/content oracles found the important defects.
118	
119	**Patterns and architectural implications**
120	
121	| Pattern | Findings | Missing enforcement | Appropriate existing responsibility |
122	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
123	| Lossy Git boundary conversions |QA-01,03,04|Filesystem identity and message data must survive Git protocol transformations|GitVcsProvider / current GitAccess boundary|
124	| Native context dropped during projection |QA-02,05|Epoch and declaring distribution must survive generic planning/rendering|VersionSpecRenderer and distribution-level graph projection|
125	| Plan authority weaker than mutation authority |QA-01|A plan must belong to the workspace/package roster it mutates|Version apply/checkpoint preparation; ApplyPermit alone is insufficient|
126	| Cache identity differs from semantic identity |QA-06|Equivalent immutable revisions should share observation work|Historical identity resolver and Git query cache|
127	
128	The existing native models already hold much of the lost information. The first corrections should be local, explicit operations and constructors that preserve it. This does not justify introducing seven new traits, replacing the synchronous runner, adding Tokio, or creating a second release workflow framework. The skill's seven responsibility names are useful ownership categories: PackageIdentityResolver, VersionSpecRenderer, ChangesetStorage, CstManifestEditor, GitVcsProvider, CascadeSolver and ReportPresenter. No new CST-fidelity or report-format defect was established in this campaign merely to fill those categories.
129	
130	Recovery needs an explicit workspace/plan binding; requirement validation needs a monotonic floor oracle in addition to target inclusion; publication projection needs a contextual edge query. These are semantic contracts worth enforcing by types/private constructors where possible. The related defect families are marked for architectural review before remediation. No remediation or spec change was performed here.
131	
132	**Prior findings, exclusions and limits**
133	
134	The ten findings in the17 November report are historical results at `ab3c030`, not ten additional current open bugs. While this campaign ran, external merges changed many of those areas. I did not perform a complete post-remediation verification of all ten and therefore do not label them all fixed or all still open. The new six were revalidated on `fac8cad` and are the current confirmed list from this campaign.
135	
136	Depth32 discovery is an explicit contract, so deeper-package omission was refuted as a new bug. The owner-cycle ambiguity is a design/spec reconciliation item. Shared-template parsing is an optimization follow-up. Known older ledger findings were excluded from new discovery.
137	
138	No live registry mutation, real forge write or full hosted workflow was exercised. Full `just ci`, current full-suite coverage, a mutation-testing campaign and all grammars/platforms were not run. This campaign uses generated tests and the existing real CLI, not comprehensive proof. Entire Brain context retrieval failed its external lock, so direct source supplied the relevant query's evidence. No automatic approval-review rejection blocked the work; the agent content-filter interruptions are recorded separately above.
139	
140	Recommended remediation order: QA-01 first, then QA-02/03, then QA-05, QA-06 and QA-04. Add boundary-level regressions with negative controls, migrate all affected sibling call sites, and run the repository's required checks on resulting changes. This report itself is not a PR readiness verdict.
141	
142	Machine-readable evidence: [finding-report.json](finding-report.json), [workspace-manifest.json](workspace-manifest.json), candidate/assessment and field-survival directories. Independent reports are under `validation-recovery/`, `validation-semantics-paths/` and `validation-architecture/`; original semantic campaign is under `semantics/`.

Not as a whole. Each WP added keys locally: named Cargo registries in #575 was the latest, and K will add Changesets translation on top. I read `docs/config.md` and our own `callisto.toml` on main.

**What's already right:** the simple case needs no config. Publish targets come from the manifests, the release trigger defaults to changesets, and changelogs default to the package directory. So the question is how steep it gets past zero.

**Where it's more complex than it needs to be:**

| Today | Problem | Simpler form, complex case kept |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publish-to = ["crates-io"]`, but the same registry is configured as `[registries.cratesIo]` | Two spellings for one thing. #575 also opened the name-clash question (a Cargo registry called `npm`) | `publish-to` names a registry. `crates-io`, `npm`, `pypi` and `github-release` are registries that already exist, and declaring one configures it. That also settles the clash without a new error code |
| `[[package]]` (exact match) and `[[package-set]]` (glob), with different allowed keys | Two concepts for one job | One `[[package]]` whose `match` accepts an exact name or a glob, with exact winning. Keys that only make sense for one package (`previous-tag-templates`) are rejected on a glob |
| One `[[release.artifact]]` block per target, each with a hand-written `asset-name` | Our own config repeats it 4+ times, and the name follows a pattern | `targets = [...]` plus an optional `asset-name` template. Explicit artifact blocks stay for irregular cases |
| `forge-repository` | Already inferred from `origin` for changelog links | Infer it everywhere; keep the key as an override |
| One-key tables (`[validation]`, `[changesets]`) | Minor | Leave them |

Fixed vs linked groups, the `[cascade]` knobs and the registry timeouts are real complexity that some users need. Their defaults are already right.

**Why now:** AGENTS.md says every key is permanent after 1.0, so this alpha is the cheapest moment. K (Changesets migration) has also not started. Settling the shape before K writes `init` translation avoids writing that code twice.

**Recommendation:** add a WP "config surface before 1.0". It starts with a short Opus design note, measured against real configs: ours, a Changesets v2 monorepo and a mixed Cargo/npm workspace. You approve the shape, then it ships as one **Breaking** changeset. `init` and an error hint migrate old keys, so existing users get one clear message rather than silent changes. K would wait for it. I'd also hold #575's reserved-name question, since the first row answers it.

These are proposals, not decided syntax. The first example is our real `callisto.toml` on main. The second is an illustrative mixed workspace, not a real repo.

## 1. This repository

**Before** (58 lines):

```toml
# callisto configuration

[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = [
    "cargo/callisto-model",
    "cargo/callisto-manifests",
    "cargo/callisto-graph",
    "cargo/callisto-cli",
    "cargo/callisto-fixtures",
]

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
forge-repository = "orin-dx/callisto"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "aarch64-apple-darwin"
asset-name = "callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"

# ... the same block four more times, for x86_64-apple-darwin,
# x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

**After** (about 20 lines):

```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["cargo/*"]

[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
targets = [
  "aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-apple-darwin",
  "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu", "x86_64-unknown-linux-musl",
]
asset-name = "callisto-{target}.tar.gz"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

What goes:
- **Five artifact blocks** become `targets` plus one `asset-name` template.
- **`forge-repository`** is inferred from `origin`, which already happens for changelog links.
- **`[changesets] dir`** and three `[cascade]` keys only restate defaults.
- **Group members** become a glob. This one is optional; an explicit list still works.

**One real catch:** we set `peer-escalation = true`. That means we kept the old v2 peer policy after N flipped the default to v3's patch policy. Is that intentional? If not, drop the line and we're on the default.

## 2. Mixed workspace (illustrative)

npm packages under `packages/`, one internal crate on a private Cargo registry, a Python package on a private index, and a CLI shipping binaries.

**Before:**

```toml
[registries.cratesIo]
confirm-timeout = "5m"

[registries.internal]
kind = "cargo"

[registries.corp-pypi]
kind = "pypi"
url = "https://pypi.corp.example/simple"

[[package-set]]
match = "npm/@acme/*"
release-trigger = "auto"

[[package]]
match = "npm/@acme/legacy"
release-trigger = "changeset"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/acme-core"
publish-to = ["internal"]

[[package]]
match = "pypi/acme-sdk"
publish-to = ["corp-pypi"]

[release]
product-package = "cargo/acme-cli"
forge-repository = "acme/tools"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/acme-cli"
target = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
```

The design note is done and saved at `.claude/plans/DESIGN-config-surface.md`. It checked each proposal against the config code: three hold up, one changes shape, and one is rejected.

| Change | Verdict | Real gain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[release] targets` + `asset-name = "tool-{target}.tar.gz"` | Yes | The only line savings: −12 on our config and on the mixed example. No JSON or wire format changes. |
| `[[package-set]]` folded into `[[package]]` | Yes | No lines saved, but it fixes a bug: `pre-major-inference` on a `[[package-set]]` is silently ignored today. I confirmed this in source. It also removes a table and a diagnostic code. |
| `publish-to` names a registry; `cratesIo` → `crates-io` | Yes, after #575 | No lines saved. It fixes another bug: `[registries.npm] kind = "cargo"` loads cleanly and only fails at release time. It also settles #575's naming question with existing error codes. |
| Infer `forge-repository` from `origin` | Yes, but my premise was wrong | It can't be an override, because every release path already requires it to equal origin's GitHub repository. Making it optional saves one line and one `init` question. |
| Globs in group `members` | No | A new package could silently join a fixed group and jump to its version. |

**Totals:** our config goes from 44 to 31 lines, the mixed workspace from 51 to 38, and a Changesets-style npm monorepo from 17 to 17. So the payoff is two bug fixes and one spelling for registries, plus shorter `[release]` blocks.

**Also found, relevant to K:**
- **npm `access`:** scoped npm packages without `publishConfig.access` publish as public. Changesets defaults to restricted, so a migration could silently make private packages public.
- **Inert registries:** a named `kind = "pypi"` registry can't be targeted by anything.
- **`nuget`:** accepted in `publish-to`, but it always fails at release.

**Rollout:** three PRs.
1. `[release]` changes. No overlap with open PRs.
2. The package fold, after #575 and #571.
3. Registry names, after #575 and the fold.

K follows the fold. The draft changeset has three **Breaking:** paragraphs and one **Action:** paragraph. No migration command is needed: old keys fail at load with a hint naming the new spelling.

**Decisions I need from you.** The note recommends:
1. Rename the wire key `cratesIo` → `crates-io` and bump the release-intent schema to 6: **yes**.
2. Keep `forge-repository` as an optional key: **yes**, so existing configs stay valid.
3. A product target listed both in `targets` and in an explicit artifact block is an error (E197), not an override: **yes**.
4. Drop `nuget` from `publish-to` until a publisher exists: **yes**.
5. Inert named npm and pypi registries: a follow-up makes them targetable like #575's Cargo ones; document them as inert until then.
6. K and Changesets `linked`: warn only, since Callisto's linked groups bump every member.
7. K and npm `access`: refuse to write without `--yes`, naming each package that would become public.
8. The owner-enforced policy script must learn to expand `targets`: **your sign-off needed**.

Go with all eight recommendations? If yes, I'll schedule the three PRs and resume Session 3 for K after the fold.

content.text:
Your CI jobs wait because of macOS runner capacity, not Callisto. Each CI run has three macOS jobs:
- the macOS test suite
- the arm64 release preflight
- the x64 release preflight

GitHub-hosted macOS runners are capped at about 5 concurrent jobs per org, and GitHub's own annotations on our runs warn that macOS arm64 is capacity-constrained. All Linux jobs in the queued runs have already finished; the runs show "queued" only because their macOS jobs are waiting. Right now 7 runs need about 21 macOS jobs, so they drain about 5 at a time.

I made it worse. Updating 7 branches at once started 7 full CI runs together, on top of the sessions' own pushes.

**What would fix it, from cheapest:**
1. **Stagger branch updates (my side, starting now).** I'll update a branch only when it's next to merge, not all at once.
2. **Run the two macOS release preflights only where they matter (your call, a CI change).** That means pushes to main plus PRs that touch build or release files: the release workflow, the templates, `Cargo.toml` and the artifact config. Every PR would keep the macOS test suite, and macOS demand per ordinary PR would drop from 3 jobs to 1.
3. **GitHub merge queue (your call).** PRs would stop needing to be up to date with main before merging. The queue tests each merge group once, which avoids re-running all of CI every time main moves.

Want me to have a session draft option 2 as a small CI PR? The workflow-policy script would need to accept the path filter too.

input.message: Lead: Entire raised 01M7RBYQ9KY9 (medium) on #571, and I'm treating it as a blocker because recovery is the release's core promise. Scenario: a v3 run archives (deletes) its source changeset, then fails writing --emit-preview or --emit-decision. The CLI keeps the checkpoint (cli commands/version.rs:191-209), and the retry re-applies the plan, but the unconditional source read fails because the source is already gone, so resume is impossible even though the archive copy is intact. Fix: make archiving idempotent. When the source is missing and the destination (including a suffixed slot) holds exactly the validated content, accept it as done. Any other missing-source case still fails. Test first: interrupt after the archive and before the emit write, then retry, and the resume succeeds with no double bump or changelog entry. Also test that a destination with different content still refuses. Push (signed, no trailer, explicit refspec, ls-remote), resolve after the push, and run mutants on the diff. After this, report any further Entire finding on #571 to me; it won't be fixed unless it breaks recovery or produces a wrong result.

content.text:
G (#571) is not ready after all. Entire found a resume bug, and Session 1 is fixing it.

- **The bug:** if a run archives a changeset and then fails writing its `--emit-*` output, resume can never succeed. That breaks the recovery promise this release is built on.
- **The fix:** archiving becomes safe to repeat. If the source is gone and the archived copy matches, resume treats the move as done.
- **Tests:** a retry must succeed with no double bump. An archived copy with different content must still be refused.
- **Further findings:** from now on, anything Entire raises on G comes to me without being fixed, unless it breaks recovery or gives a wrong result.

You can still approve these in any order now: #573 (U), #576 (W), #581 (V) and #578 (L). Merge #577 (S) after G.

Change #179 has a finding: 

<pasted_content id="cd46">
### Medium finding

**Location:** `crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs:194-198`

If a v3 run deletes its source changeset and then fails writing `--emit-preview` or `--emit-decision`, the CLI retains its checkpoint (`callisto-cli/src/commands/version.rs:191–209`). Retrying reapplies the checkpoint plan at line 186, but this unconditional read fails because the source is already gone, preventing resume despite the intact archive copy. Make archiving idempotent by accepting the validated destination when the source has already been removed.
</pasted_content id="cd46">


Is it valid or should it be dismissed?

It's valid, so keep it. This is the same finding I sent to Session 1 a few minutes ago, and Session 1 is fixing it now.

- **Why it holds:** a v3 run moves the changeset into the archive, then writes the `--emit-*` output. If that write fails, the CLI keeps its checkpoint so you can resume. But resume re-reads the original changeset, which has already been moved. Every retry then fails, and the only way out is deleting the checkpoint by hand.
- **Why not dismiss:** the release's core claim is recovery from partial failures. A resume that can never succeed breaks that claim, not just a nicety.
- **Fix:** small. If the source is gone and the archived copy matches what was validated, treat the move as done. If the archived copy differs, still refuse.
- **Verification:** Session 1 writes the failing test first, so if the scenario doesn't actually reproduce, we'll know before anything changes. After the push lands, the finding gets resolved, not dismissed.

Here is how I'd turn this session's way of working into one agent-first workstream. It's based on what broke today, not on a new framework.

**What went wrong this session:**
- Long-lived sessions stalled. Session 1 reached 787k tokens and stopped with fixes unpushed.
- Resumes failed, hit worktree locks, or sent messages to an offline remote copy.
- Codex reports arrived as pasted text that I had to re-triage by hand.
- Entire review rounds kept going, five on G.
- Branches drifted behind main, and mass updates swamped the macOS runners.
- I checked each PR against the "done" rules by hand, every time.

**The design:**

1. **One queue: Entire trails.** All work arrives as an Entire finding on the right trail: Codex audits, Entire reviews, CI failures, owner requests. Codex reports get filed as findings, not pasted. Each finding gets one triage outcome, recorded in Entire with its reason: fix now, dismiss, or backlog. The plan file keeps only work packages, owner decisions and the backlog.
2. **Short-lived workers.** Each PR or batch of findings gets a fresh session with a generated brief: the finding text, the trail, files, rules and definition of done. It ends when its PR is green. Nobody resumes old sessions, which removes the context bloat, the lock fights and the lost messages.
3. **One definition of "done", checked by script.** A small local script answers "is PR N ready?":
   - commits signed, with no session trailers
   - no `mutants.out` files
   - up to date with main, merging cleanly
   - CI green
   - no open Entire findings
   - `just ci` and mutants evidence in the PR

   Workers run it before reporting, and I run it before telling you. It lives in the local job folder, not the repo, so it adds nothing to Callisto.
4. **A triage rule instead of judging case by case.**
   - Wrong result, broken recovery, security, or a check that can't fail: fix now.
   - Otherwise: backlog with a reason.
   - Entire gets two fix rounds per PR, then everything comes to me.
5. **A merge train.**
   - Update a branch only when it is next to merge, not all at once.
   - Turn on GitHub merge queue.
   - Run the macOS release preflights only on release-relevant changes.

   Those three end the 40-minute waits.
6. **One owner digest.** You get one batched message: what's ready to merge, in order; the decisions only you can make; and what landed. Nothing else interrupts you.
7. **Optional: a Workflow per wave.** Once the queue and the readiness check exist, one Workflow script can run a whole wave as a pipeline: implement, mutants, fresh review, readiness check. It needs your explicit "use a workflow", and it costs more in tokens than single sessions.

**Order to adopt it, cheapest first:**
1. The readiness script and triage rule (local, about an hour).
2. Fresh-worker briefs generated from Entire findings.
3. The CI changes: macOS filter and merge queue.
4. Workflow-per-wave orchestration.

I can write this up as a local plan file and build steps 1 and 2 next, while G and the token-mapping PR finish. Step 3 needs your OK because it changes the repo's CI. Want me to go ahead?

Fair. I was designing machinery for us. From the user's side, the remaining work groups into the journeys someone goes through with Callisto. Each needs one test of "done" that an agent can verify, then we stop.

content.text:
The code already has the right base. Traits sit only at real seams: commands, prompts, providers, manifests and version grammars. The bugs found this week come from four places where a value loses its meaning between stages, and that is where types should do the work.

**Rules to keep:**
- **Closed sets are enums with exhaustive `match`, not traits.** Ecosystems, publish targets, distributions and version grammars are fixed lists, so a missing case should be a compile error. Codex is right that we don't need new traits.
- **Traits only where the outside world is swapped:** `CommandRunner`, `Prompter`, `ReleaseProvider`, `Manifest`. That's already the case.
- **Two stages, raw then resolved,** for config and inputs. That's also already the case.

**Where a type would have prevented this week's bugs:**

| Bug class | What happens today | Rust-native fix | Journey |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Git output trimmed or misread (QA-01, 03, 04) | Three separate `git_stdout` helpers (`checkpoint.rs`, `release_decision.rs`, `release/mod.rs`), and `literal_pathspec()` returns a plain `String` | One Git output boundary that hands back a line, a path or a list of records as distinct types. Git commands accept a `Pathspec` newtype, so a raw path can't be passed in | 5, 3 |
| Version grammar lost in range rewrites (epochs, QA-02) | `Versioning` owns bump arithmetic, but range rewriting is free functions in `python.rs` (`render_target`, `rewrite_range`) | Move range rewriting into the existing `Versioning` trait, so each grammar owns both bumping and rewriting and nothing generic sees `major.minor.patch` | 3 |
| Provisional values escape (GAP-02, the extra cascade release) | Correct only because steps run in the right order | A `ConvergedTargets` type with a private constructor that only the solver's final step can build. Rewrites, E319 checks and apply accept only that type | 3 |
| A plan applied to the wrong workspace (QA-01, T) | T checks a tree id at one call site | Build that check into `ApplyPermit`'s constructor, so every apply path gets it | 5 |
| Registry and package names (config PR 3, E) | Stringly typed in places | `RegistryName` and `NativeName` newtypes with private constructors. `NativeName` is done | 4 |
| JSON error output (agent journey) | Human text can come before the JSON | Pick the output format once, at the error renderer, so `--format json` writes only JSON | 7 |

**What I would not do:**
- An effect journal, a generic move engine, or async/Tokio. G's idempotent archive move is one case; generalize only when a second one appears.
- New traits per responsibility.

**Order, by user impact:**
1. Range rewriting into `Versioning`.
2. `ConvergedTargets`.
3. Git boundary types.
4. The permit binding.
5. JSON-only errors.

Each is one PR that deletes the per-call-site checks the new type makes redundant. None blocks the next release. The bugs they cover are already fixed by tests; this stops the same classes from coming back.

**Retrying `version` finishes when its emitted decision is inside the workspace.** A run that wrote `--emit-decision` or `--emit-preview` into `.changeset` and was then interrupted no longer refuses its own retry with `E340`.

=== .changeset/brave-lynxes-jump.md [callisto-cli: minor]
**Shorter release configuration.** List your build targets once and let Callisto name each asset, and drop `forge-repository`.

- How to adopt it: replace repeated `[[release.artifact]]` blocks for the product with `targets = [...]` and `asset-name = "tool-{target}.tar.gz"` under `[release]`. Keep `[[release.artifact]]` for another package's artifact or an irregular name such as a Windows `.zip`.
- `forge-repository` is optional: Callisto uses the `origin` GitHub repository, which every release already required it to equal.
- `callisto init` now writes `targets` and one `asset-name` template, named after the single binary or after the package when it has several.
- Limits: `{target}` is the only placeholder. A target named by both `targets` and a `[[release.artifact]]` of the product is E197.

**Breaking:** `callisto init` no longer asks for or accepts `--forge-repository`.

**Action:** drop `--forge-repository` from scripted `init` calls.

=== .changeset/brave-pandas-swim.md [callisto-cli: patch]
**Package directories with unusual names release correctly.** A package directory named with `*`, `?` or leading spaces is now read as exactly that directory.

- Commit inference and the version commit no longer pick up a sibling such as `packages/odd-other` for a package in `packages/odd*`.
- A commit message containing the U+001E control character no longer stops inference with `E026`.
- Resuming an interrupted `version` run in a workspace directory with leading or trailing spaces resumes that workspace, not a similarly named sibling.

=== .changeset/brave-panthers-climb.md [callisto-cli: minor]
**Generated release workflows publish only what a credential-free job built.** Package scripts, build backends and crate builds no longer run in the job that holds your registry tokens.

- The publish job uploads exactly the Python files and npm tarballs a job without credentials built and sealed, and publishes crates with `cargo publish --no-verify` after that job compiled every crate of the release, one `cargo package --locked` call per Cargo workspace, including a workspace under a directory such as `native/` with no root manifest.
- The simple workflow now has `version-pr`, `package` and `execute` jobs, and the build-matrix workflow gains `attest`, `package-cargo` and `pack-npm` jobs, so only `execute` holds secrets and only the attestation job holds an OIDC token without checking out your code.
- npm packages are packed by their workspace's own package manager, so `workspace:` and `catalog:` ranges are rewritten in the published tarball.
- A local `callisto release` still verifies crates and packs in place, with registry credentials withheld from the build.

**Breaking:** npm publishes now run `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`. The `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` hooks no longer run, and `prepack` and `prepare` run in the pack job, which has no registry credentials. The simple workflow now publishes only when a push adds or changes the release decision file, not whenever an untagged version is merged. A release whose npm or PyPI publish is not sealed in the artifact manifest now fails with E306 before anything is published.

**Breaking:** `npm publish <tarball>` does not read a registry set in `.yarnrc.yml` or `bunfig.toml`. A yarn workspace whose `.yarnrc.yml` sets `npmPublishRegistry` or `npmRegistryServer` (at the top level or under `npmScopes`), or a bun workspace whose `bunfig.toml` sets a registry, now fails with E168 before anything is published, and Yarn and Bun token settings are not used either.

**Action:** Yarn and Bun users: move the registry to `publishConfig.registry` in your package's `package.json`, or to `.npmrc`, and keep the publish token in `NPM_TOKEN`. Everyone: delete `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` and regenerate it with `callisto init --workflow`, then move work that must run at publish time from `prepublishOnly`, `publish` or `postpublish` into `prepack` or a step of your own after `execute`.

=== .changeset/brave-tigers-bound.md [callisto-cli: patch]
**Generated release workflows no longer open a second release PR right after a release.** After a release PR merges, the generated workflow now rebuilds the release PR only once `execute` has tagged the release.

- Packages with `release-trigger = "auto"` were affected: before the new tag existed, the commits just released were counted again and a release PR for the next version opened with nothing new in it.
- Merging that PR would have released a version with no changes. Close any such PR left open.
- Packages released from changesets were not affected.

**Large pnpm workspaces load much faster.** Relative `workspace:../path` dependencies are now resolved through one directory index instead of a scan per dependency.
